card.band: 8 h. Research class: a pass improves on the baseline. Frontier agents recall multilevel ideas and recover much of the gap, but tuning for balance at tight imbalance and large k is where they fall short of the reference. Buckets by k and imbalance. A weaker model gets small gains from refinement tweaks only.
card.cheat: Embed best-known partitions for the dev graphs: hidden graphs are different and are relabelled and permuted. Ignore balance: the checker zeroes infeasible instances. Call KaHIP or METIS: not installed, no network.
card.grading: Hidden 14 graphs not in the dev set, run at k in {2,4,8,16,32,64} and imbalance in {0,1,3,5}% (336 instances). Infeasible balance scores 0 for that instance. Otherwise score is the cut ratio to best-known, normalised between the shipped baseline and the reference. Deterministic given the fixed seed and time cap.
card.reference: Our own multilevel partitioner (heavy-edge matching, FM/KL refinement, V-cycles), about 1,500 lines, measured on the hidden graphs. It defines the ceiling.
card.source: Walshaw graph partitioning archive, mirrored as SuiteSparse DIMACS10 (https://sparse.tamu.edu/DIMACS10/cs4); 34 graphs. Licence described as public domain in secondary sources, primary statement not verified
card.task: /app ships a baseline partitioner (greedy BFS growth plus one-pass swap refinement), a graph reader, a cut and balance checker and 20 graphs with best-known cuts as the dev set. The agent designs and tunes a stronger partitioner (coarsening, initial partition, FM refinement, parameter search) and ships a CLI: graph, k, imbalance in, partition out, within a fixed CPU time per instance.

spike_plan.kill_if: No stated licence permitting shipping the graphs and no accepted substitute; or the 3-graph run is non-deterministic.
spike_plan.pass_if: A permissive licence for the graph data is found, or a self-generated substitute is accepted; the 3-graph run is deterministic and shows a measurable gap to best-known.
steps: Licence check first (about 15 min): read the LICENSE or terms of the metapart Walshaw derivative repo and the archive page; request written reuse permission from the archive maintainer. Stop if none is found.
If a permissive licence is confirmed, fetch 3 graphs (3elt, add20, memplus) from the SuiteSparse mirror in a throwaway container.
Write a ~200-line heavy-edge-matching plus greedy-refinement partitioner and run it on the 3 graphs at k in {2,8,64} and imbalance 3%.
Compare cut ratios with archive best-known values for the same cells; check determinism across 3 seeds.
If the gap to best-known is measurable and seed spread is small, the scope is viable; otherwise kill.
If no licence is found, substitute self-generated meshes or random geometric graphs from permissive generators and rescore the card.

v1.summary: The task is real and well-defined: the SuiteSparse DIMACS10 mirror lists the 34 Walshaw graphs and the archive publishes best-known cuts for the exact k and imbalance grid, so the metric is sound. It is killed under K6 because neither the SuiteSparse page nor the Walshaw archive states a licence for the graph data, and the public-domain claim only covers the archive's software, so the 20 dev graphs cannot be shipped in /app as validated.
